description: Manual complements applied by backend/scraper/apply_mapping_overlays.py after SOC reconcile. The Schedule of Classes scrape stays the rule; this file is the one place for Qatar campus additions and catalog rules on top of it. Sections run in this order, and a second run changes nothing: (1) overlays: additive requirement mappings only. (2) rule_buckets: buckets the 2026-27 catalog defines by a rule instead of a list (for example any SCS course, 200-level or above, at least 9 units). Every course row that meets a rule gets a row tagged "source": "rule", and a tagged row whose course no longer meets it is removed, so new SOC courses count from the next daily run; rows without the tag are never touched. A rule lists prefixes (two digit subject codes) with min_number and max_number, or number ranges, an optional min_units_per_course (a course passes with the most units it can carry: a 3-12 course passes 9, a VAR course falls back to its units), include (additions, always counted), exclude (deletions and excluded ranges), and non_technical where the catalog names its technical courses by list (that list is exclude); source names the archived catalog page and heading. Each rule states its number range: graduate courses (600 and above) and numbers below 100 (study abroad, internships, seminars) are left out unless the catalog's rule covers them. (3) remove_mappings: removes requirement rows for the listed programs (a list of CS, IS, BA, BS, AI or "all"); runs after (1) and (2) so nothing re-adds them, and (1) and (2) skip those programs. (4) qatar_visibility: rule show_only_if_offered_qatar sets qatar_only, and the app hides that course unless its SOC offerings include the Qatar campus. qatar_only is owned by this file: a row it no longer lists loses it. (5) campus_overrides: a course the SOC lists at the wrong campus; every SOC offering of it gets the listed campus (Qatar or Pittsburgh), and offered_qatar and offered_pitts follow. Only listed codes change. catalog_buckets lists every bucket path per program in catalog order, with the buckets that have no rows yet; each run writes it, plus any row path it lacks, to requirement_buckets.json next to the catalog, for the admin course editor. Only list what has been confirmed.
